scope: Current working tree, including pre-existing uncommitted changes. Source and native worker tests plus isolated subprocess contracts. Passing rows mean the linked checks passed, not proof of every possible input.

status_definitions.passed: Linked executed checks passed within their stated scope.
status_definitions.failed: A reproduced failure or confirmed documentation conflict exists.
status_definitions.not_verified: Required environment or evidence is unavailable; no pass claimed.

features.expected_behavior: Every public command and nested clean command has working --help with usage and flags.
--version prints sxr and the runtime package version.
Find and skills produce equivalent results through fast entry points and Typer routing.
Shared provider, project, output, time and discovery flags work before or after the command; clean also accepts group-level flags.
Conflicting providers and provider-specific discovery flags return usage errors with a useful diagnostic.
Negative row limits are rejected with exit 2, consistent with find and skills. This is a consistency expectation beyond the documented 0 and positive values.
Unexpected JSON record shapes should be skipped or reported as errors without an uncaught Python traceback. This is a resilience expectation.
--json emits parseable structured output; session read views preserve original records and never shorten values.
secrets clean honors its advertised --json flag with JSON output, or rejects that unsupported output mode. It must not silently emit TSV.
A positive -n caps JSONL record counts across show, prompts, errors and cmds while leaving each returned record intact.
The advertised -n option caps printed tools, stats, path and clean rows; zero allows all.
Bare invocation lists Claude sessions in the exact cwd, newest first, with @N handles.
--codex lists actual Codex thread IDs with kind, model/effort, counts and source metadata.
List -n caps visible sessions, -n 0 shows all, and text output reports omitted sessions.
Sessions whose last timestamp is within ten minutes of now are labelled live; JSON has a separate boolean.
An empty list currently returns exit 0 and no JSON rows; stderr explains searched roots. This deliberate tested exception conflicts with the README's general empty=1 statement.
Only displayed sessions are summarized; titles and metadata refresh on later invocations.
No session argument selects the newest session in the filtered scope.
@N selects one session; @A:@B includes both endpoints and accepts reverse order.
Unique ID prefixes and case-insensitive name/title matches resolve sessions; unknown or ambiguous selectors fail with exit 2.
Ambiguity diagnostics identify candidates, cap them at five short titles, and preserve distinct conflicting source paths.
Claude child IDs are parent-qualified and Codex child IDs remain real thread IDs with parent lineage metadata.
--path expands ~, resolves relative paths and symlinks, and defaults to one exact recorded project.
--recursive includes descendants without matching sibling paths that merely share a prefix.
--worktrees adds registered sibling Git worktrees and is opt-in for both providers.
Repeated --claude-root searches multiple profiles; explicit roots replace CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; Codex roots come from CODEX_HOME.
Ordinary session views require --include-agents for Claude children; nested child cwd follows recorded metadata and parent fallback.
Ordinary Codex views include archived_sessions only with --archives; active/archive conflicts remain distinguishable.
Byte-identical copies of a session collapse into one result with all provenance paths; conflicting copies remain separate.
--coverage reports searched and unavailable roots on stderr without corrupting JSON stdout; empty/multi-root discovery also reports roots.
--file skips discovery, detects either provider from records, preserves exact source/child identity, and constrains all session commands.
An explicit file rejects inconsistent optional ID, project, provider or profile flags, missing files and conflicting selections.
Legacy Claude files without cwd can still match the full encoded project directory.
--since is inclusive and --before exclusive; dates and ISO timestamps are interpreted as UTC instants. Fractional precision and recorded offsets must not change membership.
today means UTC midnight; @N uses that session's start; filters renumber the remaining handles.
Invalid dates and handles return exit 2 with accepted forms; an empty window explains what was excluded.
Printed follow-up commands preserve exact files, provider, absolute project/root paths and source coordinates when run from another cwd.
The default skeleton shows text, tool calls and turn context; hidden kinds are named with recovery flags.
--thinking includes reasoning, --tools includes results, --errors selects recorded failures, and --type selects exact or dotted kinds.
--around and --context select events by original physical line number and print whole selected text.
--range accepts inclusive A:B and A-B spans; malformed values return exit 2 with syntax help.
--tail N returns the last N selected events in order and prints whole text.
--tail 0 means zero events, distinct from the specifically documented -n 0 unlimited convention. This boundary expectation is inferred.
--full includes all event kinds and prints whole text, as the help epilog and installed primer promise.
Broad show/prompts scans print whole text under the budget, trim explicitly above it, and honor --budget/--line-limit over SXR_BUDGET/SXR_LINE_LIMIT.
No matching selected records returns exit 1 regardless of JSON/text rendering.
Claude prompts exclude metadata and compaction summaries; Codex prefers explicit user_message events and otherwise uses recorded user content labels.
Unlabelled legacy user-role text remains available; duplicated legacy user-message forms do not produce repeated prompts.
--all includes every user-role event, including injected context, attachments and tool results.
cmds prints recorded tool command text and paired ok/err/unknown outcomes for Claude and Codex.
cmds --grep searches full untruncated command text across the scope with smart-case regex behavior, not command output.
The command-row limit applies across selected sessions; -n 0 shows all and truncation is reported.
Bad --grep regexes exit 2 and name the flag and literal escape fix.
Errors preserve original flagged records and denial kinds; repeated representations of one Codex outcome are not counted twice.
Claude isApiErrorMessage records counted in session errors should also be retrievable through errors and show --errors.
errors -n caps records across the whole range and reports omissions.
tools counts calls and failures by tool from parsed records.
Each Skill call contributes once to the count for its own input.skill, even when several tool calls share a physical record.
stats reports per-property record counts, tokens, model, errors, interruptions and attribution from recorded data.
path prints selected source paths including Claude child files; --file returns only that explicit file and requires no full transcript parse.
grep searches decoded event text with smart-case regexes; -i forces any case, -F is literal, and -e permits a leading dash.
-C emits symmetric surrounding event windows without exceeding the global row cap; -A/-B teach the supported flag.
-c counts matching events per session, ranks by matches, reports first source event, and prunes zeros unless --all is set.
--sort started returns oldest matching sessions first; invalid sort values return exit 2.
-l prints one selector per matching session.
Match rows are capped by -n or the character budget; -n 0 lifts both caps, --budget 0 lifts the budget, and the true total is reported.
No matches returns 1 with a scope hint; missing/invalid patterns return 2 with recovery advice rather than an empty-result status.
find defaults to both providers, Claude children and Codex archives; project/provider filters narrow that union.
All clues must match somewhere in the same session; --any accepts any clue; quoted phrases must occur within one event.
Matching is case-insensitive, normalizes most Latin diacritics and punctuation, and treats FTS syntax as data.
Ranked hits include source coordinates and up to three bounded excerpts that actually show the matched text, including normalized matches.
Ranked search defaults to five sessions, -n changes the limit and zero returns all; total counts logical deduplicated sessions.
--paths skips ranking/excerpt reads, returns sorted physical paths including copies, defaults to all, and uses paths in JSON.
CODEX_THREAD_ID takes precedence over CODEX_SESSION_ID; current Codex files are excluded unless --include-current or explicit --file selects them.
Repeatable --exclude-session excludes full session IDs for either provider and reports excluded-file counts in coverage.
Every request checks inventory and source identity; additions, appends, rewrites, replacements and deletions change subsequent results.
Missing requested roots, incomplete metadata and sources changed during search set complete=false and exit 2; unstable results are withheld.
--index prepares the ranked index; find requires caching and errors with recovery instructions on unavailable or corrupt cache data.
Warm inventory does not parse unchanged transcripts; only displayed results load excerpt bodies and cached tool outcomes remain canonical.
index builds search data within the selected provider/project scope; --clear removes search, ranked, catalog and read caches.
Caches respect SXR_CACHE_DIR and XDG_CACHE_HOME, default to ~/.cache/sxr, and are created with owner-only access.
Literal searches of at least three characters use the index; short patterns and regex operators use direct reads with identical outputs.
Escaped and normalized Unicode remains searchable without incorrect candidate exclusions.
Verified appends decode only new records; partial final lines are revisited; edits and same-mtime replacements invalidate stale data.
Unavailable, locked, corrupt or unsupported caches fall back to direct grep/read results; cache faults never masquerade as no matches.
Catalog migrations preserve warm results and scope filtering precedes construction of unrelated references.
Zooms cache positions and seek only selected physical records while retaining whole-session outcomes and event counts.
Any source change rebuilds read positions and earlier tool outcomes; concurrent mutation falls back or prevents publication of an unstable snapshot.
Blank, torn, invalid UTF-8 and supported line endings preserve source event coordinates across direct and cached reads.
Modern completed command items and legacy function-call outputs retain command, output, exit/status and line numbers; stable IDs deduplicate representations without merging separate executions.
Audit scans selected session credentials, including values in recorded tool inputs such as Write.content, and returns a masked rotation worklist.
Bundled text rules, provider prefixes, URL credentials, JWT validation, password assignments and private-key recognition distinguish certain/probable findings from placeholders.
--candidates opts into entropy review findings; candidates and hexadecimal noise are excluded by default and overlap keeps the strongest finding.
Neither text nor JSON exposes credential values; fingerprints are stable and salted and worklists aggregate occurrences and session spread.
-n limits the worklist and reports omitted findings without misrepresenting the full distinct-secret count.
secrets audits by default, accepts a session selector or audit subcommand, and exposes clean as a nested command.
secrets clean is a dry run unless --apply is supplied; preview scans the same selected files without rewriting them.
Apply rewrites only certain/probable credentials with redaction markers, leaves no backup, and is idempotent; an already-clean scope exits 1.
Cleaning finds decoded JSON string credentials, nested/serialized JSON, whole structured passwords, duplicate members, escaped text and multiline private keys.
Property names, unrelated values, untouched bytes, invalid lines and line endings survive; replacements are longest-first and do not alter protocol metadata.
Cleaning includes selected provenance copies and Claude children once per physical file; explicit --file selects no extra copies or children.
Each physical file's recent activity is checked independently; timestamps within ten minutes of now cause a skip, including nested children.
Changed files are replaced atomically with original permissions after identity, size and timestamp checks; concurrent writes cause an error and remain intact.
Files without findings need no temporary copy; failed temporary files are removed and cleanup failures are reported.
Cleaning follows a selected symlink to the physical target while preserving the symlink and avoiding duplicate work.
File errors and decode failures return exit 2 without a traceback; unrelated selected files can still be processed.
Apply clears derived transcript caches before and after the rewrite and refuses changes if the first clear fails.
Unsupported bundled rules stop scanning rather than silently reducing coverage; all bundled rules compile with correct captures and flags.
Discover SKILL.md recursively across configured roots including hidden, repository, dependency and external config locations; only sxr's own cache is excluded.
Repeated --root selects roots; --index --root remembers them; lookup-only roots use a separate map; --defaults restores home discovery.
Follow directory symlinks once per physical directory, skip cycles, retain aliases without counting them as extra copies.
Queries match case-insensitive directory/path clues; --exact requires a whole directory name and qualified clues filter locations before grouping.
SHA-256 groups byte-identical instruction files, retaining copies and locations; different contents stay distinct and supporting assets are not compared.
--paths prints canonical representatives; --copies expands matching files; --aliases adds aliases for returned files without increasing copies.
Text/JSON default to 20 groups, paths defaults to all, -n limits results, zero lifts the cap, and totals remain accurate.
JSON includes skills, total, unique, files, complete, errors, coverage, indexed_at, cycles_skipped and index path.
Warm lookups validate matching files without rediscovery; edits are rehashed before grouping; new installations require --index.
Reindex omits vanished paths, old poisoned maps repair stale missing-file diagnostics, and changed/deleted matching paths request a reindex.
Missing explicit roots, permission errors, changing hashes and retargeted aliases report incomplete discovery and exit 2; ordinary lookup diagnostics are bounded.
Transient changes while hashing are retried; stable file signatures reuse hashes on reindex.
The map persists across upgrades, migrates supported old versions, rebuilds corrupt data and is replaced atomically.
--clear removes the default map and remembered roots; SXR_NO_CACHE scans without saving a map.
Invalid combinations such as --aliases without --paths, --exact without a query and conflicting clear/root/default flags return exit 2.
Bare init emits the versioned primer without modifying instruction files.
--write chooses the nearest AGENTS.md walking upward, creates one in cwd if absent, or respects an explicit file.
--global chooses existing ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, then ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, then ~/AGENTS.md.
--write appends/replaces only the marked block, preserves neighboring prose, and becomes byte-identical on a second invocation.
--check returns 0 for the current version, 1 for missing/stale blocks, and reports version drift.
Unbalanced, reversed or repeated primer markers return exit 2 and leave the file untouched.
--write/--check and --global/explicit-file conflicts are rejected; a file argument alone does not guess whether to write.
Destination filesystem errors produce a useful diagnostic with exit 2 instead of an uncaught traceback.
The native launcher starts a local worker for find/skills, reuses its PID and SQLite pages, and observes edits and cleared caches.
Each request forwards its own cwd, provider roots, cache settings and current-session identity, including unset values.
Concurrent starts and relocated launchers work; SXR_NO_DAEMON and failed worker startup fall back to direct execution.
serve status reports worker PID/version, serve stop releases it, and the worker expires after idle timeout.
The socket is owner-only; oversized/malformed requests and unexpected environment keys are rejected.
Explicit skill reindexing runs separately so lookups continue through the existing worker.
A freshly built macOS arm64 archive relocates successfully and works without system Python or Homebrew on PATH.
features.verification_note: Built current sources and ran packaging/verify.py after relocation on this host with an empty PATH. See evidence/build.log and evidence/bundle.log.

features.expected_behavior: macOS x86_64 and Linux arm64/x86_64 archives run on the documented macOS/Ubuntu hosts.
features.verification_note: No Linux or x86_64 host is available in this audit. The documented macOS 14/15 and Ubuntu 22.04 compatibility matrix was not rerun.

features.expected_behavior: The Homebrew formula installs/updates the matching prebuilt bundle without compiling a Python/OpenSSL dependency chain.
features.verification_note: No Homebrew install/upgrade was performed. The fresh local archive was tested independently of any published formula or release.

features.expected_behavior: Published 0.8/0.9 benchmark measurements remain historical measurements; this working tree's performance against those baselines requires the original corpus and protocol.
features.verification_note: Historical RTK/rg timing claims were not rerun against their private 738-file benchmark corpus. Functional cache and worker tests are separate evidence.

features.expected_behavior: The global exit-code reference accurately describes empty results, including the intentional empty-list exception.
path honors its advertised --json mode with structured paths or rejects that unsupported option.

issues.title: Secret audit misses credentials in Write tool contents
issues.expected: The masked audit finds credentials stored in a recorded Write.content value.
issues.observed: The synthetic Write call contains a password assignment. secrets --json exits 1 with no finding. secrets clean previews one replacement in the same file.
issues.impact: A rotation worklist can incorrectly report a clean session containing a stored credential. The same omission can affect other tool input fields hidden by the display summary.
acceptance: Scan relevant decoded record values rather than only display summaries
Keep credential values out of text and JSON output
Add a test asserting that audit and clean agree on this Write fixture

issues.title: Time filters compare timestamp strings instead of instants
issues.expected: Session membership follows the UTC half-open interval [since, before), independent of timestamp precision and offset spelling.
issues.observed: A session at 12:00:00.123Z is excluded by --before 12:00:00.123001Z. A session at 13:00:00+02:00 is excluded by --before 12:00:00Z even though it started at 11:00 UTC.
issues.impact: Searches can omit the requested historical sessions or include sessions outside a time boundary.
acceptance: Normalize both stored timestamps and bounds before comparing
Check inclusive since and exclusive before for equivalent offsets and mixed fractional precision
Preserve @N and today semantics

issues.title: Counted Claude API errors disappear from the errors view
issues.expected: A Claude isApiErrorMessage record counted as an error can be inspected with errors and show --errors.
issues.observed: list --json reports errors=1 for the fixture, while errors --json returns no records and exits 1.
issues.impact: The aggregate error count points to a failure that the dedicated error view cannot retrieve.
acceptance: Carry isApiErrorMessage into canonical error annotations
Return the original failed record in errors and show --errors
Keep list and stats error counts consistent
issues.requirement_basis: Consistency between counted record properties and the errors command

issues.title: Normalized find matches can produce excerpts with no matching text
issues.expected: The excerpt for a normalized match shows the original source occurrence, including diacritic-insensitive matches.
issues.observed: Query cafe matches a long event ending in café, but the returned excerpt contains only its leading padding. The match lies beyond the excerpt because position lookup uses unnormalized substring search.
issues.impact: Agents receive a correctly matched session with evidence that does not demonstrate why it matched.
acceptance: Locate excerpt spans using tokenization compatible with ranked matching
Retain a mapping to original source character positions
Test long events with diacritics and normalization differences

issues.title: show, prompts and errors ignore row limits in JSON mode
issues.expected: -n 1 returns at most one JSONL record, keeping that record complete.
issues.observed: The fixtures return 7 records from show, 3 from prompts, and 2 from errors with --json -n 1. cmds honors the same combination.
issues.impact: Consumers cannot bound these read responses and may load an entire large transcript unexpectedly.
acceptance: Apply row selection limits before JSON serialization
Keep returned records unmodified
Report omissions through stderr or a documented metadata channel
Verify -n 0 still returns all records

issues.title: errors applies text limits per session and hides omissions
issues.expected: The errors -n limit applies to the entire selected scope and a shortened view states the omitted count.
issues.observed: errors @1:@2 -n 1 prints two error rows. A single session with two errors prints one row but only reports a total of two errors, without stating one row was omitted.
issues.impact: Range scans exceed the requested budget and users can mistake a shortened list for the complete set of failures.
acceptance: Track a scope-wide emitted-row count
Show a precise omitted-record notice
Cover multi-session and single-session limits

issues.title: tools, stats, path and clean accept but ignore -n
issues.expected: Commands that advertise a printed-row limit honor it, or reject an unsupported option.
issues.observed: With -n 1, tools prints two tool rows, stats prints 17 field rows, and path prints both parent and child paths. A clean preview also prints both selected file rows with -n 1.
issues.impact: The shared option appears valid while providing no control over these outputs.
acceptance: Implement consistent row limits with omission notices or remove unsupported command options
Preserve explicit-file scope and unlimited zero semantics

issues.title: --full still trims long transcript text
issues.expected: --full prints whole text, as both the help epilog and agent primer state.
issues.observed: show --full trims a synthetic user message larger than the default 40,000-character scan budget. --around correctly preserves the full text.
issues.impact: An agent following the documented recovery flag still loses content.
acceptance: Treat --full as disabling text trimming, or consistently change the published contract
Add a long-record CLI check distinct from ordinary full-kind selection

issues.title: Skill input counts multiply when calls share a record
issues.expected: Two Skill blocks calling notify and review produce one input count for each.
issues.observed: calls reports Skill=2, but skill_inputs reports notify=2 and review=2. Each Skill event rescans all tool_use blocks in the original physical record.
issues.impact: Per-skill usage reports overcount batched tool calls.
acceptance: Associate each event with its own input block or count each physical block once
Test two Skill calls plus an unrelated tool in the same record

issues.title: Empty show selections exit successfully only in text mode
issues.expected: An empty selection returns exit 1 regardless of output format.
issues.observed: show --type does-not-exist exits 0, while the same command with --json exits 1.
issues.impact: Scripts that use the documented exit code treat missing evidence as a successful result.
acceptance: Return the same empty-result status for text and JSON
Check empty type, range and around selections

issues.title: --tail 0 returns the entire selected transcript
issues.expected: Last zero events produces an empty selection; only -n 0 is documented as unlimited.
issues.observed: Python's [-0:] slice returns the complete selection, so --tail 0 --json emits every skeleton record.
issues.impact: A computed zero tail count can unexpectedly print a large transcript.
acceptance: Handle zero explicitly or reject it with documented usage guidance
Validate negative tail counts
Keep positive tail order unchanged
issues.requirement_basis: Inferred boundary behavior from 'Last N selected events' and the separate -n 0 convention

issues.title: Negative row limits are accepted inconsistently
issues.expected: A negative row count is a usage error, as already enforced by find and skills.
issues.observed: list, show, prompts, errors, tools, stats and cmds all accept -n -1 and exit 0. Some slice off a row, some emit none and some ignore the value.
issues.impact: A malformed calculated limit silently changes output instead of reporting the mistake.
acceptance: Validate shared limits centrally as integers >= 0
Apply validation at every supported flag position
Retain the documented zero meaning
issues.requirement_basis: Inferred consistency requirement with existing find/skills validation

issues.title: path and secrets clean accept --json but emit plain text
issues.expected: An accepted --json option emits structured output, or the command rejects the unsupported option.
issues.observed: The clean command advertises --json, accepts it and exits 0, but stdout contains a TSV header, data row and dry-run prose. path --json likewise accepts the option and returns a plain pathname.
issues.impact: Automation piping a clean preview to a JSON reader fails despite using an accepted flag.
acceptance: Implement JSON output for preview/apply results or reject the flag clearly
Keep diagnostics separate and credential values masked

issues.title: Limited secret worklists understate the number of findings
issues.expected: A worklist limited with -n reports the full distinct count and number omitted.
issues.observed: Two different synthetic password values are detected. With -n 1, the footer says '1 distinct secrets' and provides no omitted-count notice.
issues.impact: A user can stop rotating credentials after the one displayed row because the summary hides the remaining finding.
acceptance: Compute totals before slicing
Report shown, total and omitted counts
Keep returned fingerprints stable across limited and unlimited views

issues.title: A non-object JSONL record crashes transcript reads
issues.expected: A structurally invalid record is skipped or reported through a controlled error without losing source-coordinate integrity.
issues.observed: A valid user record followed by JSON number 42 makes show --full exit 1 with an AttributeError traceback rather than a diagnostic.
issues.impact: One malformed record can make otherwise readable session evidence inaccessible and is reported using the documented empty-result exit code.
acceptance: Validate decoded record shapes before accessing mapping fields
Keep later valid records readable or clearly mark the read incomplete
Apply the same policy to both providers and cache parsing
issues.requirement_basis: Resilience expectation based on supported malformed/torn JSONL handling

issues.title: Primer filesystem failures escape as Python tracebacks
issues.expected: An invalid or unwritable destination returns a useful filesystem diagnostic with exit 2.
issues.observed: init --write not-a-directory/AGENTS.md, where not-a-directory is an existing regular file, exits 1 with a FileExistsError traceback.
issues.impact: Setup automation receives the empty/stale status for a real write error, with an unnecessarily long exception dump.
acceptance: Catch relevant filesystem errors at the command boundary
Report the destination and error on stderr
Keep the original file intact

issues.title: The documented empty-result exit code omits the list exception
issues.expected: The exit-code reference clearly describes list returning 0 for an empty scope, if that deliberate exception remains.
issues.observed: README and top-level help say exit 1 means an empty result. list_scope explicitly returns 0 for an empty scope, and test_empty_json_list_keeps_stdout_machine_readable asserts that behavior.
issues.impact: Consumers following the global exit-code description cannot infer whether an empty listing is a miss or a successful command.
acceptance: Document the empty-list exception in the README and help, or adopt a consistent behavior after reviewing compatibility
Keep the primer exit-code guidance consistent with the chosen rule
issues.requirement_basis: Documentation consistency, confirmed by the existing empty-list CLI test

Print the primer that teaches agents sxr, or install it in a context file.

between <!-- sxr:primer vX.Y.Z --> markers in FILE (default: the nearest
